thread:
maria: FYI — canary rollout of the route-weighting change (routing-proxy v2) just produced a small but consistent invoice-preview spike for ~40 tenants. digging in now.

 tom: ugh — spike = how big? tokens or duplicate events?

 maria: looks like duplicate token events on fallback paths. samples show the same request emitted twice to the metering producer when proxy falls back to route-v2. not a huge cardinality, but enough to move invoice previews for a few tenants.

 alex: is there an idempotency key? we rely on X-Request-ID + tenant to de-dupe downstream. do we preserve it on retries/fallbacks?

 maria: nope — that's the smoking gun. proxy retry fanout path creates a new request id on fallback. example log snippet: 

 ```
 2026-03-20T12:00:01Z proxy-123 INFO handle_request tenant=acme request_id=rid-01 route=route-a fallback=false
 2026-03-20T12:00:01Z proxy-123 WARN retrying fallback to route-v2 tenant=acme new_request_id=rid-01-1
 2026-03-20T12:00:01Z metering-producer INFO emit tenant=acme request_id=rid-01 tokens=34
 2026-03-20T12:00:01Z metering-producer INFO emit tenant=acme request_id=rid-01-1 tokens=34
 ```

 nina: so metering sees two distinct request_ids -> double-count. can we make the proxy preserve the original X-Request-ID across fallback and retries?

 maria: that's the proposed fix. quick patch to routing-proxy: when fallback is triggered, set X-Request-ID = original if present. also add a small integration test.

 mike: adding de-dupe in ingest layer is also an option, but that's heavier — we'd need to keep an in-memory minute window and check (tenant, request_id). that may add latency/coordination cost.

 alex: prefer making the source (proxy) correct. de-dupe in ingest is fallback for older clients that don't send X-Request-ID.

 tom: what's the impact on dashboards/console? support will see spiky invoice previews. we should add a temporary console card showing "fallback-invocations" per route so support can triage quickly.

 nina: I can add a metric to the console: routing.fallback.count by route and tenant. small feature flag so we don't expose broadly. will wire to trace links.

 sara: good — customers asked for better visibility into fallbacks during rollouts. +1 from product.

 deploy-bot: canary deployment routing-proxy v2 started at 2026-03-20T12:00:00Z (canary cluster: canary-us-west-2)

 maria: plan: 1) revert the canary (so previews stop moving), 2) patch proxy to preserve X-Request-ID and add unit/integration tests, 3) add console fallback metric behind feature flag, 4) consider ingest-level de-dupe for telemetry-poor clients.

 tom: recommend revert now. shadow canary until we validate header preservation.

 maria: initiated revert. deploy-bot should post status.

 deploy-bot: revert routing-proxy v2 canary initiated at 2026-03-20T12:03:30Z — canary traffic draining.

 alex: after patch, let's add a tiny telemetry field on metering events: upstream_request_origin = proxy|edge|sdk so we can filter double-count risk in analytics.

 nina: console card will also surface upstream_request_origin so support can filter in invoice-preview.

 mike: implementation note — ingest de-dupe (if we add) should only dedupe exact request_id matches within a 2-minute sliding window and only for non-streaming calls to avoid complexity.

 maria: timeline: revert done, patch PR opened (https://git.internal/redwood/routing-proxy/pull/1723), will cut canary (shadow) with header-preserve logs tomorrow morning and flip feature flag after a +12h soak.

 tom: thanks — assign someone to run a quick backfill check on invoice-preview diffs once canary is clean.

 sara: I can coordinate support comms and add a note in the console "we saw an internal routing change that affected invoice previews temporarily" once we confirm root cause.

 maria: thanks all. will follow up with postmortem if the preview deltas were > $100/day aggregated.

 tom: ack.

 nina: I'll post the console card PR link when ready.

 maria: closing thread for now, will re-open if we see more anomalous previews.
